prompt: On an Ephemery node an eth_simulateV1 request never returned, and block import stalled for about 11 minutes until we restarted. The request had a blockOverrides.number far beyond the head. Find why our 256-block limit did not stop it, and any similar unbounded inputs in that method. Read-only.

expected.gold_summary: The gap is narrowed with (targetNum - prevNum).toInt before the 256-block check; a gap of 2^32+1 wraps to 1, so the check passes and the gap loop builds ~2^32 blocks on the RPC thread. Fix: compare as BigInt (geth sanitizeChain), bound the loop itself, -38026 'too many blocks'; also the per-block 5000 and total 10000 call limits, 256/64-bit bounds on override quantities judged before BigInt parsing, and decodeErrorString's .toInt on the revert length.

rubric: Points at the Int narrowing of the block-number gap before the 256-block comparison in EthSimulateService
Explains the 2^32 wrap that lets a huge gap pass as small
Proposes a BigInt comparison and/or a loop-level bound matching geth sanitizeChain
Finds at least one other unbounded input: call counts, override quantity width, or the Error(string) length .toInt
